first matching function or a specific listener by its unique id.
  - This allows proper removal of once-listeners and precise control when needed.
- Fixed emit to handle removals during emission and avoid skipping
  - emit now snapshots the listeners registered at the start of the emit.
  - It only calls listeners that were present at the start (by matching IDs).
  - If a listener is removed before its turn, it’s skipped.
  - Listeners added during an emit will run only on the next emit.
  - Once-listeners are removed immediately after being invoked.
- Types and structure
  - Introduced ListenerEntry with a unique id for each listener.
  - Updated internal storage to Map<string, ListenerEntry[]>.
  - Ensured compatibility with existing tests (off(event, fn) still works; once takes a new path; tests for multiple registrations still hold).

Files touched
- src/emitter.ts
  - Replaced the simple function-based storage with a robust, id-based ListenerEntry model.
  - Implemented on, once, off, emit with the described semantics.

Usage notes
- once(event, fn) returns an unsubscribe function similar to on, but the listener will only be invoked once.
- off(event, fn) continues to work as before, removing the first matching listener for that function.
- Listeners added during an emit will not run in the current emit; they will run on the next emit.

If you want, I can add a dedicated test for once to ensure it fires only once and is properly unsubscribable via the returned function.
